title: Delhi Police rescue 72 Malaysians held by an online-scam syndicate in Noida, India
date_note: Kosmo (published 27 November) says the raid took place on Thursday, which is 26 November.
geo_basis: city: Kosmo says the raid took place in Sector 136, Noida
summary: Kosmo Malaysia reports that Delhi Police raided a suspected cyber-scam syndicate in Noida and rescued 72 Malaysians. Joint Commissioner Surender Kumar said police acted on information a Malaysian sent by email. Utusan Malaysia reports the victims were allegedly lured by job offers, had passports taken and were forced to run online scams; a 25-year-old Malaysian was detained.
plain: Delhi Police raided a suspected online-scam operation in Noida and rescued 72 Malaysians. Utusan Malaysia reports they were allegedly lured by job offers and then made to run online scams.
exec: Police in India raided a suspected online-scam syndicate and rescued 72 Malaysians, Kosmo Malaysia reports; investigators are reportedly tracing the money flow.

validation.note: Kosmo Malaysia and Utusan Malaysia each report the rescue of 72 Malaysians by Delhi Police; Kosmo quotes the police Joint Commissioner. The Sun (Malaysia) was also read but its page shows no publication day, so it is not cited.
